subject: bio
source: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus for examination in 2026, 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Year 11 covers topics 14–21 plus full-course revision for the May/June exams

weeks.topic: Coordination and response: the nervous system and neurones
objectives: Describe the central and peripheral nervous system
Identify sensory, relay and motor neurones
Compare nervous and hormonal control

weeks.topic: Reflex arcs and synapses
objectives: Describe a simple reflex arc and why reflexes are important
Explain how impulses cross a synapse using neurotransmitters

weeks.topic: Sense organs: the eye, pupil reflex and accommodation
objectives: Label the structures of the eye and state their functions
Explain the pupil reflex in changing light
Describe accommodation for near and distant objects

weeks.topic: Hormones: adrenaline, insulin, glucagon and the endocrine glands
objectives: Define hormone and identify endocrine glands
Describe the effects of adrenaline
Name hormones produced by the pancreas, testes and ovaries

weeks.topic: Homeostasis: blood glucose and body temperature control
objectives: Explain negative feedback in homeostasis
Describe how insulin and glucagon control blood glucose
Explain thermoregulation by sweating, vasodilation and shivering

weeks.topic: Tropic responses: phototropism, gravitropism and auxin
objectives: Define phototropism and gravitropism
Investigate tropic responses in seedlings
Explain the role of auxin in shoot growth

weeks.topic: Drugs: antibiotics and antibiotic resistance
objectives: Define a drug and describe the use of antibiotics
Explain why antibiotics do not affect viruses
Describe how antibiotic-resistant bacteria such as MRSA develop

weeks.topic: Asexual and sexual reproduction
objectives: Define asexual and sexual reproduction with examples
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of each
Describe haploid gametes and diploid zygotes

weeks.topic: Sexual reproduction in plants: flowers and pollination
objectives: Identify the parts of insect-pollinated and wind-pollinated flowers
Compare self-pollination and cross-pollination

weeks.topic: Fertilisation in plants and the conditions for germination
objectives: Describe pollen tube growth and fertilisation
Investigate the conditions needed for seed germination

weeks.topic: Sexual reproduction in humans: reproductive systems and fertilisation
objectives: Label the male and female reproductive systems
Compare sperm and egg cells
Describe fertilisation and implantation

weeks.topic: Fetal development and the placenta
objectives: Describe the functions of the placenta, umbilical cord and amniotic fluid
Explain how some pathogens and toxins cross the placenta

weeks.topic: Sex hormones, the menstrual cycle and sexually transmitted infections
objectives: Describe changes at puberty caused by hormones
Explain the roles of FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone
Describe how HIV is transmitted and controlled

weeks.topic: Chromosomes, genes and protein synthesis
objectives: Define chromosome, gene and allele
Describe how DNA codes for proteins
Outline transcription and translation using mRNA and ribosomes

weeks.topic: Review: coordination, homeostasis, drugs and reproduction
objectives: Revisit nervous and hormonal control and homeostasis
Practise reproduction diagram and data questions

weeks.topic: Mitosis, meiosis and stem cells
objectives: Describe mitosis for growth, repair and asexual reproduction
Describe meiosis as reduction division producing variation
Explain the role of stem cells

weeks.topic: Monohybrid inheritance and genetic diagrams
objectives: Use Punnett squares and genetic diagrams
Define genotype, phenotype, dominant, recessive, homozygous and heterozygous
Use test crosses and pedigree diagrams

weeks.topic: Codominance, blood groups and sex-linked inheritance
objectives: Explain codominance using ABO blood groups
Describe how sex is determined by X and Y chromosomes
Explain sex-linked inheritance such as colour blindness

weeks.topic: Variation and mutation
objectives: Compare continuous and discontinuous variation
Describe gene mutation and factors that increase mutation rate
Explain sickle-cell anaemia and malaria

weeks.topic: Adaptive features, natural selection and selective breeding
objectives: Describe adaptations of xerophytes and hydrophytes
Explain natural selection and evolution
Compare natural and artificial selection

weeks.topic: Energy flow, food chains, food webs and ecological pyramids
objectives: Describe energy flow from the Sun through food chains
Construct food webs and pyramids of numbers, biomass and energy
Explain energy losses between trophic levels

weeks.topic: Nutrient cycles: the carbon and nitrogen cycles
objectives: Describe the carbon cycle including photosynthesis, respiration and combustion
Describe the nitrogen cycle including the roles of bacteria

weeks.topic: Populations: growth curves and factors affecting population size
objectives: Identify the phases of a sigmoid population growth curve
Explain factors such as food supply, predation and disease

weeks.topic: Human influences on ecosystems: food supply, habitat destruction and pollution
objectives: Describe the impacts of monocultures and intensive livestock farming
Explain effects of deforestation
Describe eutrophication and the effects of non-biodegradable plastics

weeks.topic: Conservation: sustainable resources and endangered species
objectives: Explain sustainable resource use in forestry and fishing
Describe conservation methods such as seed banks, breeding programmes and protected areas

weeks.topic: Biotechnology and genetic modification
objectives: Explain why bacteria are useful in biotechnology
Describe uses of enzymes, yeast and fermenters
Outline the process and uses of genetic modification

weeks.topic: Mock exams: full syllabus (multiple choice, theory and practical papers)
objectives: Complete full-length mock papers under exam conditions
Analyse mock results to build a personal revision plan

weeks.topic: Review: characteristics, classification, cells and movement into and out of cells
objectives: Recall key definitions and cell structures
Practise magnification and osmosis calculations

weeks.topic: Review: biological molecules, enzymes and plant and human nutrition
objectives: Revise food tests and enzyme graphs
Practise photosynthesis limiting factor and digestion questions

weeks.topic: Review: transport in plants and animals, diseases and immunity
objectives: Revise heart, blood vessels and transpiration
Practise immunity and data interpretation questions

weeks.topic: Review: gas exchange, respiration, excretion, coordination and homeostasis
objectives: Revise respiration equations and the nephron
Practise nervous system and homeostasis long answers

weeks.topic: Review: drugs, reproduction, inheritance, variation and selection
objectives: Practise genetic diagrams and probability
Revise reproduction and natural selection explanations

weeks.topic: Review: ecology, human influences, biotechnology and practical skills
objectives: Revise food webs, nutrient cycles and conservation
Practise planning investigations and drawing graphs for the practical paper

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: multiple choice paper (Paper 1 or 2)
objectives: Answer 40 multiple-choice questions with good time management
Use elimination strategies for difficult questions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: theory paper (Paper 3 or 4)
objectives: Answer structured and extended questions using precise biological terms
Interpret unfamiliar data and diagrams

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: practical or alternative to practical paper (Paper 5 or 6)
objectives: Plan investigations, identify variables and control them
Draw tables, graphs and biological drawings accurately

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on the course and next steps for IB or A Level Biology
